streaming = watching or listening to media over the internet as it is sent
paywall = a system that allows only paying users to read or watch content
influencer = a person who promotes products or views to a large online following
headline = the title of a newspaper article, printed in large letters
editorial = an article that gives the newspaper's own opinion
investigative journalism = reporting that uncovers hidden facts, often over a long period
correspondent = a journalist who reports from a particular place or on a particular topic
press conference = a meeting where someone answers journalists' questions
exclusive = a story published or broadcast by only one news organisation
fake news = false stories presented as news, often to mislead or attract clicks
misinformation = false or inaccurate information, whether spread on purpose or not
clickbait = a sensational headline designed to make people click, often misleading
sensationalism = presenting stories in an exaggerated way to shock or excite
freedom of the press = the right of newspapers and broadcasters to report without unfair control
prime time = the evening hours when the largest television audience is watching
readership = the people who regularly read a newspaper or magazine
paparazzi = photographers who aggressively pursue celebrities for pictures
podcast = a spoken audio programme you can download or stream in episodes
going viral = spreading extremely quickly across the internet
echo chamber = an online space where you only meet opinions you already agree with
